items.title: GiatMARA instructor killed, 2 children injured in Alza-lorry crash in Sabah
items.summary: KOTA BELUD: A GiatMARA instructor was killed and her two teenage children were injured after Perodua Alza car collided with a lorry along Jalan Kota Belud-Tuaran near Taman Nikmat. Kota Belud police chief Superintendent Khairul Shah Peri said preliminary investigations showed the lorry, driven by a 42-year-old man, was heading from Kota Belud towards Tuaran. Khairul said the victim's body was sent to the Kota Belud Hospital forensic unit for further action.

items.title: Algae growth turns Pertang River green, says Fisheries Dept
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Excessive algae growth caused by prolonged hot weather and a lack of rainfall has turned the river water in Mukim Pertang, Jelebu, green. The Negri Sembilan Department of Fisheries (DOF) director Kasim Tawe said investigations found the colour change was not caused by pollution, but by green algae growth in nearby fish ponds due to the hot weather. Kasim said fish breeders should take several measures to control algae growth, including using waterwheels at night, changing the water gradually, reducing feeding, installing shading nets, applying probiotics, and reducing the fish population in the ponds.

items.title: Madinah: Different audit methods led to contrasting AG, PwC findings on TH
items.summary: She said the audit was conducted under the Audit Act and Tabung Haji Act, with the objective of determining whether TH's financial statements presented a true and fair view in accordance with the Malaysian Financial Reporting Standards (MFRS), particularly MFRS 139. In contrast, she said PwC's review was conducted as a "Financial Position Review", a special assignment with different terms of reference and a broader approach to assessing TH's financial position. "The audited financial statements showed a net profit of about RM3.4 billion, while PwC's Financial Position Review reported a deficit or loss of about RM1.4 billion.

items.title: #NSTviral: Johor-Singapore bus driver braves rain to confront queue-cutting motorists [WATCH]
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: A Johor-Singapore bus driver braved heavy rain to confront several motorists who allegedly cut the queue and used a dedicated bus lane to overtake other vehicles at the Customs, Immigration and Quarantine (CIQ) Complex here. Bus drivers plying the Johor Baru-Singapore Causeway daily often honk continuously in frustration when motorists use the dedicated bus lane to jump the queue before cutting back into the line heading towards the Bangunan Sultan Ismail CIQ. However, one driver took a different approach.

items.title: Elderly woman allegedly killed over home renovation fee dispute
items.summary: SANDAKAN: A dispute over a home renovation fee allegedly led to the murder of a 62-year-old woman, whose body was found dumped in a toilet at her house in Jalan Leila, Tanah Merah. The suspect allegedly assaulted and strangled the woman before dumping her body in the toilet, according to a source. The source said neighbours noticed a foul stench coming from the house several days later and notified the police at 8pm last Wednesday.

items.title: Marang Prison inmate beaten to death by 3 prisoners over old debt
items.summary: MARANG: A 38-year-old inmate at Marang Prison was beaten to death yesterday by three prisoners over a dispute. Marang police chief Superintendent Sofian Redzuan said the victim was brought to the Merchang health clinic for treatment but was confirmed dead on arrival. He said three inmates, aged 21, 35 and 35, were identified as the suspects who attacked and beat the victim.

items.title: Man arrested over theft, burning of Quran copies in Senawang
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Police arrested a man at a hotel in Chow Kit, Kuala Lumpur, yesterday to assist in investigations into the theft and burning of copies of the Quran. Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the 25-year-old suspect was arrested following a public complaint about a fire near a field in Senawang on Aug 22. "Investigations revealed that the fire involved several copies of the Quran.

items.title: High Court slashes man’s rape sentence from 10 years to one, citing youth and rehabilitation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — The High Court in Kuantan has slashed a man’s sentence for statutory rape from 10 years’ imprisonment and six strokes of the cane to one year’s jail and two strokes. In allowing the 23-year-old’s appeal against the penalty, Judicial Commissioner Samry Masri ruled that the Sessions Court had failed to give adequate weight to the accused’s youth, his clean record as a first offender, and his strong prospects for rehabilitation, FMT reported. The Sessions Court had handed down five years’ imprisonment and three strokes of the rotan for each charge, ordering the sentences to run consecutively.

items.title: Putin allows Russia to take control of infrastructure deemed vulnerable to drone attacks
items.summary: MOSCOW: President Vladimir Putin on Monday handed the Russian state the power to take control of critically important infrastructure if it is deemed to be poorly protected from Ukrainian drone attacks and other threats. The special powers, set out in a presidential decree, will allow the state to take over temporary administration of such facilities at a time when Ukraine has stepped up drone attacks on oil refineries and retail warehouses. On Monday, Russia's second-largest online retailer Ozon, said four of its logistics hubs in southern Russia had been targeted in Ukrainian attacks.

items.title: Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore reaffirm commitment to keep key straits safe
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Malaysia, Indonesia and Singapore have reaffirmed their shared commitment to keeping the Straits of Malacca and Singapore free, open and safe for international shipping. Meanwhile, Singapore Transport Minister Jeffrey Siow said the Straits of Malacca and Singapore (SOMS) were a primary artery for global trade, with more than 100,000 vessels passing through the waterways each year. "In our part of the world, we will endeavour to keep the Straits of Malacca and Singapore free, open and safe for international shipping," he said during the opening of the forum.

items.title: Fire crews gain ground on destructive blaze raging near Reno, Nevada
items.summary: RENO: Firefighters logged major gains on Monday against a wind-driven blaze that threatened the city of Reno, Nevada, over the weekend, destroying dozens of houses and chasing tens of thousands of people from their homes. As of Monday, fire crews had managed to carve containment lines around 27 per cent of the Hawk Fire, which erupted on Saturday near Nevada's third-most-populous city and raced through tinder-dry grass, brush and forest into residential areas. It was the second major wildfire to strike Nevada's Truckee River valley area in recent weeks.

items.title: Police: Plantation supervisor seriously injured in machete attack at workers’ quarters in Gua Musang
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 25 — A plantation supervisor was seriously injured after being attacked by a group of individuals armed with machetes, iron rods and wooden clubs during an altercation at a workers’ quarters in Kampung RKT Kesedar Chalil, Gua Musang, yesterday. Gua Musang police chief Supt Sik Choon Foo said the incident occurred at about 3.15pm after a group of men, believed to be representatives of a company with interests in the area, arrived at the quarters to seek clarification regarding permits to enter a forest reserve. A plantation worker who attempted to intervene was subsequently attacked by the group using weapons such as machetes, iron rods and wooden clubs,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Sunway founder confirms Sunway Lagoon roller coaster incident
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sunway Group founder Tan Sri Jeffrey Cheah has confirmed Saturday night's roller coaster accident at Sunway Lagoon. He said authorities were investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident. Yesterday, Subang Jaya district police chief Assistant Commissioner Wan Azlan Wan Mamat said 10 riders suffered minor injuries.

items.title: MetMalaysia issues thunderstorm, heavy rain warning for 10 states, 3 Federal Territories
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain, and strong winds across 10 states and three Federal Territories until 5pm today. The Federal Territories affected are Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya, and Labuan. In Peninsular Malaysia, the affected states comprise Perlis, Kedah, Penang, and Selangor (Kuala Selangor, Klang, Kuala Langat, Petaling, Gombak, Sepang, and Hulu Langat).

items.title: Zahid backs PAC move to probe Tabung Haji management since 2017, stresses facts over perception
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi supports a proposal for the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) to establish a special body to investigate the management of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) from 2017 to the present. Ahmad Zahid said the investigation was important to clarify what had happened after 2017 based on facts and reality, while also helping to correct public perceptions regarding TH’s management and governance. Asked whether the proposal to establish the special body would be brought to the Cabinet, Ahmad Zahid said this was unnecessary as the PAC has the appropriate mandate and responsibility to conduct the investigation.

items.title: Malaysia’s SMART rescue team prepares for United Nations reclassification, aims to retain status
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 25 — The Malaysian Special Search and Rescue Team (SMART) is determined to retain its Heavy Urban Search and Rescue (Heavy USAR) classification under the United Nations (UN) as a special “gift” to Malaysia in conjunction with the 69th National Day celebrations. SMART Team Commander PgKB I Abdul Manaf Che Isa said the country’s elite rescue team is scheduled to undergo the INSARAG External Reclassification (IER) assessment from Sept 20 to 24 to retain the classification, which it first obtained in 2016. Abdul Manaf expressed confidence in SMART’s level of preparedness after undergoing three large-scale pre-IER exercises, including one simulation last year and two this year.

items.title: PN, Umno call for new RCI to investigate TH
items.summary: PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said this was necessary as findings from the previous RCI report on TH had been used to manipulate the narrative and portray the agency as having been embroiled in a major financial scandal. Also present were Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, Wanita Umno chief Datuk Seri Dr Noraini Ahmad, Puteri Umno chief Datuk Nurul Amal Mohd Fauzi and Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki. Meanwhile, Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Mohd Razlan Rafii also supported the establishment of a new RCI to investigate TH's financial affairs after the previous RCI.

items.title: Slight haze relief as unhealthy areas drop from 32 to 29
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Nationwide haze conditions showed slight improvement, with 29 areas recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 2.30pm today, compared with 32 areas this morning. The Batu Muda monitoring station in Kuala Lumpur recorded a reading of 154, followed by Nilai (154); Sungai Petani (153); Pegoh Ipoh (153); Kuala Selangor(153); and Sarikei (153). A total of 38 monitoring stations recorded moderate readings, with none registering very unhealthy or hazardous levels.

items.title: Lee Lam Thye urges urgent review of Asean haze pact, calls for enforceable action plan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Asean leaders have been urged to conduct an urgent high-level review of the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution and adopt a stronger, time-bound and enforceable regional action plan to prevent the haze situation from worsening. Social activist Tan Sri Lee Lam Thye said the recurring transboundary haze crisis could no longer be treated as a seasonal inconvenience, saying that Asean must move from reaction to prevention and strengthen regional preparedness. “We must stop treating haze as an annual Asean ritual.

items.title: Stray elephant in Kampung Jeram relocated to Royal Belum State Park
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: A female elephant that had been roaming around Kampung Jeram, Manir, since last Friday was successfully relocated by the Terengganu Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) today. Its director, Dennis Ten, said the elephant was captured and rescued on Saturday. He said the relocation operation began at 8am today and involved 13 Terengganu Perhilitan personnel, seven staff from the Sungai Deka Elephant Conservation Centre and two personnel from the National Elephant Conservation Centre in Kuala Gandah.

items.title: Man arrested in Chow Kit hotel over Quran burning, theft investigations
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 25 — Police arrested a man at a hotel in Chow Kit, Kuala Lumpur, yesterday to assist investigations into the burning and theft of copies of the Quran. Negeri Sembilan Police Chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the 25-year-old suspect was arrested following a public complaint about a fire near a field in Senawang on Aug 22. “Investigations revealed that the fire involved several copies of the Quran.

items.title: Strong winds hamper efforts to battle 51.4ha peat fire in Kota Tinggi
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI: Hot weather and strong winds are hampering efforts to put out a 51.4-hectare peat fire along Jalan Bypass Sebana Cove-Punggai that broke out yesterday. Operations commander Deputy Fire Superintendent II Baharuddin Idris said 9.7 per cent of the 35.6-hectare fire in Sector A, as well as the entire 15.8-hectare Sector B, was under control. "Our main challenges are strong winds, hot weather and limited water supply.

items.title: Hot weather and strong winds complicate firefighting as 51‑hectare Kota Tinggi peat blaze rages
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Aug 25 — Hot weather and strong winds are complicating efforts to put out a 51.4-hectare peat fire along Jalan Bypass Sebana Cove-Punggai that started yesterday. Operations commander, Deputy Fire Supt II Baharuddin Idris said 9.7 per cent of the fire in Sector A, which is 35.6 hectares, and the entire area of Sektor B (15.8 hectares), was under control “Our main challenges are strong winds, hot weather and limited water supply. Fire and Rescue Department personnel battling the blaze along the Punggai–Sebana Cove bypass.

items.title: PAC to discuss proposal for special body to review TH management tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) will discuss a proposal to establish a special body to review the management of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) from 2017 onwards. PAC chairman Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin said the matter would be discussed with committee members after its proceedings in Parliament tomorrow. "Tomorrow, PAC has proceedings in Parliament.

items.title: Thousands join Maulidur Rasul nationwide, Anwar leads UPM procession under Madani Dihayati theme
items.summary: At the national level, the celebration at Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM), Serdang was attended by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, with more than 4,000 people, including procession contingents. Also present were Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (JAKIM) director-general Datuk Dr Sirajuddin Suhaimee. Also present were Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, State Secretary Datuk Dr Ahmad Fadzli Ahmad Tajuddin, Selangor Islamic Religious Council chairman Datuk Salehuddin Saidin and State Islamic Religion and Cultural Innovation Committee chairman Dr Mohamad Fahmi Ngah.

items.title: Sultan Nazrin honours 82-year-old mother of 15 with family award
items.summary: IPOH: Raising 15 children while living a modest life was never easy for Yang Walad, but her faith, patience and prayers helped her see them through to adulthood. Yang said she never expected to receive the award, especially from the Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah. I worked in the padi fields while raising my children.

items.title: Zahid wants PAC to probe management of TH after 2017
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) should establish a special body to investigate the management of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) from 2017 to the present, says Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. The deputy prime minister said the move was important to enable the body to clarify the true situation regarding TH after 2017, based on facts. Zahid said this would help correct public perception regarding TH's management and governance issues.

items.title: Man with disabilities reports loan shark harassment over unpaid loans
items.summary: CHERAS: A person with disabilities (PWD) said he has faced almost daily harassment from loan sharks since last month over unpaid loans exceeding RM17,000 taken through money lending apps. He said each loan was subject to a high service transaction fee. Even though I said I will repay the money, they still harass me every day," he said.

items.title: Miti to drive low-altitude economy development with unmanned valley ecosystem project
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry will implement the Unmanned Valley Ecosystem pilot project to drive the development of the low-altitude economy (LAE). LAE refers to economic activities and public services conducted within a low-altitude airspace ecosystem using technologies such as drones, advanced air mobility, air logistics, infrastructure inspection, smart farming, and emergency services. Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin said the project would be carried out under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP), with the proposed pilot project to be located at universities.

items.title: Kuantan port eyes liquid cargo diversification, to handle 30mil tonnes of liquefied CO2 annually by 2050
items.summary: Kuantan Port chief commercial officer Mazlim Husin said the port has collaborated with Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) on carbon capture and storage, which could see liquid cargo playing a more important role at the port. He said Petronas has signed an agreement to lease or sublease about 60 hectares (ha) at Kuantan Port for the development of a terminal. "We have a collaboration with Petronas at Kuantan Port.

items.title: Philippines seeking to expand military drone capabilities, says defence chief
items.summary: MANILA: The Philippines plans to expand its unmanned capabilities, including through development and acquisition of drones as part of efforts to modernise its military, its defence chief said on Tuesday. US defence ally the Philippines also plans to acquire additional guided-missile corvettes and other major defence assets to beef up its external defence capabilities, Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro told a budget hearing in the lower house of Congress. The armed forces currently operate a fleet of unmanned aerial vehicles that provide intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance, Teodoro said.

items.title: Malaysians advised to reconsider non‑essential travel to Pattani, Yala and Narathiwat amid unrest
items.summary: KANGAR, Aug 25 — Malaysians in Pattani, Yala and Narathiwat, as well as those planning to travel there, have been urged to remain vigilant following a series of recent security incidents in the three southern Thai provinces. Malaysia’s Consul General in Songkhla, Thailand, Ahmad Fahmi Ahmad Sarkawi, said those planning to travel to the affected areas were advised to reconsider non-essential travel. “Malaysians are also advised to avoid areas affected by security incidents, demonstrations or large gatherings and to comply with instructions from the Thai authorities, including those on curfews, road closures and security checks,” he said in a statement from Istana Arau today.

items.title: Prime Minister urges Muslims to reflect Prophet’s values, not limit Maulidur Rasul to celebrations
items.summary: SERDANG, Aug 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the commemoration of Maulidur Rasul should not be limited to celebrations or processions, but should instead be reflected through practising Prophet Muhammad’s (PBUH) way of life as a source of mercy and guidance for all humanity. He said the Maulidur Rasul celebration should serve as a platform to inspire Muslims with renewed spirit, awareness and enlightenment. Every episode in the life of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) offers a lesson for us,” he said in his speech at the national-level Maulidur Rasul 1448/2026 celebration here today.

items.title: Khee San chairman steps down after six bank accounts frozen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Khee San Bhd's largest shareholder Datuk Seri Ngu Tieng Ung stepped down as executive chairman on Monday due to personal reasons, the company said in a Bursa Malaysia filing. Ngu holds a 27.18 per cent indirect stake in the confectionery company through his private vehicles, Heritage Winners Sdn Bhd and Juarastasi Amad Sdn Bhd. His resignation came three days after Khee San announced that six bank accounts belonging to its subsidiary Khee San Food Industries Sdn Bhd had been frozen following an investigation under anti-money laundering laws.

items.title: BN's partner for Melaka polls may be decided at Aug 28 Umno meet
items.summary: MELAKA: Barisan Nasional's partner for the upcoming Melaka election may be known after the Umno Supreme Council meeting on Aug 28. Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh said the issue of political cooperation is expected to be among the key items on the agenda. Previously, BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi indicated that the understanding between BN and Perikatan Nasional would continue in Melaka.

items.title: Malaysia carves premium niche in Asia's digital-infra race – Economist
items.summary: Juwai IQI global chief economist Shan Saeed said Malaysia's data-centre boom is beginning to look less like spillover from Singapore and more like a distinct economic strategy. He said the investment numbers are increasingly macroeconomically consequential and Malaysia already possesses a sizeable digital base. Shan said the policy challenge is to convert infrastructure investment into domestic value-added and productivity growth.

items.title: 2017 audit found no direct theft at TH, says former auditor general
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Tan Sri Dr Madinah Mohamad has denied that there were elements of direct theft at Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) during her tenure as auditor general. She said the 2017 Auditor General's Report did not identify any evidence of direct theft at TH when the document was prepared by her and her team. "I did not see any such evidence (of theft at TH) when I was the auditor general.

items.title: CAP urges action over erosion, pollution at Penang beach
items.summary: BAYAN LEPAS: A consumer watchdog has called for immediate action over coastal erosion and marine pollution affecting Tanjung Asam beach in Gertak Sanggul. Consumers' Association of Penang (CAP) president Mohideen Abdul Kader said a recent survey found significant changes to the beach over the past year, including toppled trees, damaged shelters and increasingly polluted seawater. He said the beach, once known for its clean, clear waters and white sand, was now affected by polluted seawater and blackened sand.

items.title: Trees 'giving up': Climate change hammers historic English gardens
items.summary: AT Hampton Court Palace, head gardener Graham Dillamore strode across the burnt beige grass in the spectacular formal gardens southwest of London, laid out in the 17th century. "If we have a summer like this next year, by God, it's going to be a struggle," said Dillamore, who has spent more than 20 years tending the gardens of the Baroque and Tudor red-brick palace where King Henry VIII once caroused. They're not going to come back, they're finished," said Dillamore, who also oversees gardens at Kensington Palace, the official London residence of Prince William and his wife, Catherine.

items.title: Dayang earnings poised to rebound in FY27 after weak FY26
items.summary: AmInvestment Bank Bhd said Dayang's core earnings of RM54.8 million for 1H FY26 missed expectations, accounting for 24 per cent of its full-year estimate and 30 per cent of consensus estimates. Marine charter pre-tax earnings plunged 82 per cent as Perdana swung to an RM8.4 million loss, while Dayang's topside maintenance services profit fell 30 per cent on slower work order conversion. AmInvestment Bank expects Dayang's topside maintenance services order-book conversion to rise to 16 per cent in FY27 and marine charter utilisation to improve to 74 per cent.

items.title: Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore reaffirm commitment to free and safe Strait of Malacca
items.summary: SINGAPORE, Aug 25 — Malaysia, Indonesia and Singapore reaffirmed their shared commitment to keep the Strait of Malacca and Singapore Strait free, open and safe for international shipping. The commitment was made by the Malaysia Marine Department, Indonesia’s Directorate General of Sea Transportation, and the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) in a joint statement issued during 17th Co-operation Forum on Tuesday. Meanwhile, Singapore Transport Minister Jeffrey Siow said the Straits of Malacca and Singapore (SOMS) are a primary artery for global trade, with more than 100,000 vessels passing through the waterways each year.

items.title: Anwar: Amirudin tasked to work out Pakatan-BN alliance details for Melaka polls
items.summary: SERDANG, Aug 25 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari has been given the mandate to work out the details of proposed cooperation between the coalition and Barisan Nasional (BN) for the Melaka state election, said PH chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar, who is also the prime minister, said Amirudin had been entrusted with looking into the matter. he said.

items.title: Sultan Nazrin calls for less political rivalry among Malaysia’s Muslim leaders
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 25 — The unity of Muslims is facing growing challenges due to differences in politics, religious schools of thought, race and personal interests, Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Shah said. “These include Islamic economics, Islamic finance, the halal industry, waqf, digital dakwah and strengthening family institutions. Also present were the Raja Permaisuri of Perak Tuanku Zara Salim, Perak Raja Muda Raja Jaafar Raja Muda Musa and Raja Di Hilir Raja Iskandar Dzurkarnain Sultan Idris Shah.

items.title: Prime Minister confirms Felda forensic audit proposal will be tabled at Cabinet meeting soon
items.summary: SERDANG, Aug 25 — A proposal for a forensic audit to be conducted into the management of the Federal Land Consolidation and Rehabilitation Authority (Felda) will be discussed by the Cabinet, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar was responding to a question about Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s suggestion that a forensic audit be conducted to determine whether there had been abuse of power, breach of trust or governance violations in Felda’s management. Previously, Anwar said he would await the full report by the special task force investigating Felda’s management issues before making any official announcement.

items.title: Immigration lodges police report after viral UTC Pudu post found inconsistent with CCTV records
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 25 — The Immigration Department of Malaysia (JIM) has lodged a police report over a viral post concerning an applicant’s experience at the UTC Pudu Sentral Immigration Branch Office. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said a review found that several allegations in the post were inconsistent with closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage, related records and statements from officers on duty at the time of the incident. A police report has been lodged and JIM will provide its full cooperation to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM),” he said.

items.title: Haze alert: Penang health exco advises face masks as API levels spike
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 25 — Residents of Penang are urged to limit outdoor activities as air quality deteriorated today, with three of the state's four monitoring stations breaching the unhealthy threshold. State youth, sports and health committee chairman Daniel Gooi advised the public to wear face masks when outdoors to mitigate the effects of the poor air quality. According to the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), readings as of 11am showed unhealthy levels across most of the state.

items.title: MACC probes RM80m Felda Palong 7 oil palm replanting scheme after settlers raise concerns
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) is examining information related to the implementation of the oil palm development and replanting programme at Felda Palong 7 in Wilayah Raja Alias, Bandar Sri Jempol, Negeri Sembilan, including concerns over the quality of the seedlings supplied and their compliance with the required specifications. In a statement, MACC said the information was received from Pertubuhan Badan Bertindak Generasi Palong (Perbagi) chairman Mohd Syahrizal Md Yusuf, who raised concerns over the quality of the oil palm seedlings and the implementation of the programme. The commission said the matters raised included the supply, delivery, storage and age of the oil palm seedlings, as well as whether they complied with the required specifications.

items.title: MetMalaysia warns of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds across four states and Sarawak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Four states in Peninsular Malaysia and Sarawak are expected to experience thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds until 1 pm today, according to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia). In Selangor, the areas forecast to be hit are Kuala Selangor, Sabak Bernam, Hulu Selangor and Gombak, while in Sarawak, the areas involved are Bintulu and several areas in Miri, namely Subis, Miri, Beluru and Marudi. Meanwhile, in a separate statement, MetMalaysia also issued a Tropical Storm Advisory (NARRA) after a tropical storm was detected in northwestern China today, but stressed that the phenomenon would not have a significant impact on Malaysia.

items.title: Civil Defence Force vows safety review after trained sergeant dies from cobra bite
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — The Malaysia Civil Defence Force (APM) takes the fatal snakebite incident involving one of its personnel seriously and remains open to reviewing and improving safety measures, risk management and the implementation of activities from time to time. APM also confirmed that the 39-year-old was a trained personnel, with extensive experience in handling venomous animals and had been actively serving since 2010. “APM stresses that the venomous animal handling activity was carried out in accordance with the stipulated standard operating procedures (SOPs) and safety procedures.

items.title: Sarawak and Klang Valley worst hit as 30 spots in Malaysia breach ‘Unhealthy’ API levels
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Malaysia’s prolonged haze crisis showed no signs of abating today, with 30 monitoring stations nationwide recording “unhealthy” Air Pollutant Index (API) levels, according to data from the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS). Sarawak remained the epicentre of the country's worst air pollution. The IPD Serian monitoring station recorded the highest reading nationwide at 180, inching toward the “very unhealthy” threshold of 201.

items.title: Anwar reflects on Prophet’s leadership, promises change and justice for Malaysia in Maulidur Rasul message
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that he will continue striving to bring about change and reform ( islah ) for the country, taking the strategy of Prophet Muhammad SAW in establishing a new administration in the Arab region over 14 centuries ago as a reference. This resolve is a prerequisite for ensuring the essentials (daruriyat) in Maqasid Shariah, as expressed by Muhammad Imarah,” he said. In the same post, Anwar also shared the history and hardships faced by Prophet Muhammad SAW in establishing a new administration in the Arab region over 14 centuries ago.

items.title: Anwar applauds Sukma 2026 champions, urges youth to chase glory and carry Malaysia’s name worldwide
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari and the state government for their commitment and hard work in successfully hosting the 2026 Malaysia Games (Sukma). He also congratulated the athletes, coaches, officials and secretariat involved, saying Sukma was not merely about winning medals but also a platform for discovering talent and producing champions. Even sweeter, hosts Selangor emerged as the overall champions of Sukma 2026,” he said in a Facebook post last night.

items.title: IKEA picks Kuching for first-ever small store format in Malaysia, eyes December opening
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — IKEA Malaysia has confirmed that its first store in East Malaysia will open its doors in Kuching this December, marking a significant expansion into Sarawak after years of serving the state solely through e-commerce and delivery. IKEA Malaysia revealed that the new outlet will be the retailer's first small-format store, building on IKEA's existing e-commerce and fulfilment presence in the state. IKEA Kuching will become the company's fifth physical store in Malaysia, joining IKEA Damansara, IKEA Cheras, IKEA Tebrau and IKEA Batu Kawan.

items.title: MetMalaysia warns of sustained hot spell, 17 areas nationwide placed under caution status
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) today issued a Level 1 (caution category) hot weather status for 17 areas across Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak. In a statement, MetMalaysia said 11 of the affected areas are in Peninsular Malaysia, involving Larut and Matang, Kuala Kangsar, Kampar and Batang Padang in Perak; Kuala Krai in Kelantan; Kuantan, Raub, Temerloh and Pekan in Pahang; as well as Hulu Selangor and Gombak in Selangor. MetMalaysia said the Level 1 hot weather alert is issued when the maximum daily temperature in an area reaches between 35 and 37 degrees Celsius for at least three consecutive days.

items.title: Police say Pasir Mas crash kills elderly woman and granddaughter, third victim hospitalised with injuries
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 25 — An elderly woman and her granddaughter were killed after the Perodua Axia they were travelling in veered off the road and crashed into a tree along Jalan Pasir Mas-Rantau Panjang near Culvert 5 in Pasir Mas yesterday. In the 11.20 am incident, the 73-year-old woman, who was seated in the rear, died at the scene, while her 23-year-old granddaughter, who was seated in the front, died while receiving treatment at Pasir Mas Hospital. Pasir Mas district police chief ACP Mazlan Hassan said the car was driven by another granddaughter of the victim, an 18-year-old girl, who suffered a fractured wrist and internal injuries and is receiving further treatment at the same hospital.

items.title: Will Tian Chua contest Batu again? Returning PKR veteran eyes political revival
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Former PKR vice-president Tian Chua has set his sights on a return to Parliament and is open to contesting his former stronghold of Batu, citing enduring grassroots support from the constituency. Tian Chua represented Batu for two consecutive terms after winning the seat in 2008. Despite the political fallout, Tian Chua claimed that his ties to the grassroots remain intact.

items.title: Police confirm Kajang road closures as Merdeka Eve celebration rehearsals roll out
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Five main roads around Kajang will be closed in stages from this Wednesday before being fully closed on Aug 30 in conjunction with the 2026 Selangor State Merdeka Eve Celebration at Kajang Stadium. Kajang District Police Chief ACP Naazron Abdul Yusof said the road closures were aimed at ensuring smooth traffic flow and public safety throughout the programme scheduled for Aug 30. He said Jalan Mahkamah would be fully closed from Aug 26 to 30, while four other roads — Jalan Cempaka Putih, Jalan Cempaka Kuning, Jalan Stadium and Jalan Cheras — would be closed in stages.

items.title: Ten arrested in Sandakan after woman found bound, murdered in home
items.summary: SANDAKAN, Aug 25 — Police have arrested 10 suspects, including two primary individuals, following the brutal murder of a 62-year-old woman whose decomposing body was discovered bound inside a toilet in Tanah Merah, Jalan Leila, last Tuesday. Sandakan District Police Chief ACP George Abd Rakman confirmed the discovery. “The discovery was made after police received information from the public at around 8.10pm regarding a foul smell coming from the house.

items.title: Selangor marks Sukma victory with Sept 1 holiday, honouring athletes and 10,000 volunteers
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 25 — The Selangor government has declared Sept 1 as a special holiday to commemorate the state contingent’s success in winning the overall title at the 2026 Malaysia Games (Sukma), held in Selangor. Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari announced the decision at the Games’ closing ceremony at Aneka Walk, SA Sentral, here yesterday, adding that it was a token of appreciation from the state government to the entire Selangor contingent for bringing honour to the state. Amirudin also expressed his appreciation to all parties who supported the Selangor contingent throughout the Games.

items.title: Worth the bargain? Malaysian consumers win big on Pinduoduo as local sellers cry foul
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 —Inside the sprawling digital storefront of Chinese e-commerce titan Pinduoduo, Shaun Kong routinely finds exactly what he didn't know he was looking for. He uses it to purchase routine lifestyle items—clothing, accessories, and unbranded goods. Is this Chinese dumping?
